scope: Transport switch race observed in the native WebView; distinct from shared-memory throughput and game task logic.

preFixObservation.firstSolve: Frontend callback timed out after 30 seconds.

selectedEvidence.event: Data initialization starts during an explicit WebSocket switch.
Provider, sync, and trigger report no authenticated session and request recovery.
Backend is stopped again after readiness.

findings: Closing business/control channels exposed authenticated with no session; automatic init could start recovery during the explicit switch.
Old initialization waits/finally and inbound messages lacked a complete generation boundary.

Heartbeat recovery retained the previous connection age and could run before authentication or a fresh heartbeat grace period. Individual recovery callers were not recorded, so the third restart is not attributed solely to the watchdog.
changes: Control teardown atomically changes authentication phase; explicit switching suppresses automatic init/recovery.
Initialization/retries/inbound messages are generation-aware; stale waits cancel and old finally blocks cannot change the new generation.
Successful switches start initialization after releasing the switch guard.
The heartbeat watchdog refreshes grace when mode/authentication/heartbeat changes and only recovers authenticated WebSocket connections.
Control-channel heartbeat and auth_revoked messages also require the active control identity and generation.
regressions: Real store with automatic initialization and concurrent recovery starts only one backend per switch.
A delayed old init cannot clear a new init flag or report stale readiness.
A native switch initializes without a component/probe invoking init on its behalf.
Clock-driven watchdog tests cover same-mode reconnect, zero heartbeat, authentication phases, and polling that must not extend grace.
A retired control cannot refresh the new heartbeat or revoke the new authenticated connection.
